title: ropeway:handbook-title-50
text: An aerial ropeway carries a cabin across ground you would rather not walk. A haul rope is strung from tower to tower, the cabin hangs from it on a grip, and it runs end to end and back again. The words Tower - the gantry you build. Every tower is the same structure; a tower with only one span attached is an end tower, and that is where the cabin stops. There is no separate station block. Span - one straight stretch of haul rope between two towers. Line - all the towers and spans chained end to end. Footing - the pylon footing on the ground. It is the tower: it validates the build, owns the spans and takes every click. Sheave - the grooved wheel in the pylon head that the rope runs through, four blocks above the footing. Grip - the clamp on top of the cabin that holds it to the rope. Building a tower Place a pylon footing on the ground where the tower should stand. It turns to face you, and the whole tower is measured up from it. Look at the placed footing - while the tower is unfinished the block info panel names the two directions the cabin will pass through, so you can turn the footing down the line before building anything. You then place thirteen more blocks by hand: - Two posts of four blocks, standing on the ground two blocks either side of the footing. Wood or dressed stone: logs, debarked logs, planks, raw stone, cobblestone, drystone, polished rock or stone bricks, so the tower can match whatever you build in. Slabs, stairs and soil are not posts. - A five-wide crossarm across their tops, four blocks up: the pylon head directly above the footing with two ropeway braces either side of it. That is the whole tower - one crossarm, one block deep. It leaves a clear three-wide, four-tall archway, and the cabin threads through it nose first with its mast in the sheave. Right-click the footing at any time. If the tower is unfinished it tells you how many blocks are missing and lights up every cell that is wrong or empty - red where the wrong block sits, and the colour of the block it wants where nothing is. Every other click a tower takes lands on the footing too; the pylon head up top is only a piece of the frame. Sneak and right-click the footing to open the tower guide: the build order in words, next to a turning 3D view of the three blocks the tower is made of and of the cabin itself. Next: Building a Line.
